paper_metadata.title: Comparative study on microstructures and mechanical properties of ultra ductility single-phase Nb40Ti40Ta20 refractory medium entropy alloy by selective laser melting and vacuum arc melting

evidence.quote: Single-phase BCC Nb40Ti40Ta20 (NTT) refractory medium entropy alloy (MEA) was prepared by selective laser melting (SLM) and vacuum arc melting (VAM).
The microstructure and mechanical properties of Nb40Ti40Ta20 MEA prepared by selective laser melting (using element powder blends) and vacuum arc melting were compared in this work

evidence.quote: The Nb-Ta-Ti mixed powders were homogenized for 12 h by a mixer at the speed of 200 rpm using a stainless steel mixing tank in a protective Argon atmosphere and dried at 120 ℃ for 6 h in the vacuum atmosphere.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the alloy was fabricated by a DiMetal-150 Selective Laser Melting system, which was equipped with a 500 W fiber laser, the spot diameter of 20 µm, and argon (Ar) as protective atmosphere, Oxygen content less than 100 ppm, forming substrate using pure titanium substrate and preheated to 200 ℃.
Therefore, the laser parameters of E = 381.9 J/mm3 were used to prepare the NTT alloy to analyze the microstructure and mechanical properties in this study.

evidence.section: 2.2 Raw materials and alloy manufacturing methods
evidence.quote: NTT alloy was prepared in a water-cooled copper crucible in an arc melting furnace. In order to ensure the uniformity of chemical composition, each button ingot was re-melted for 6 times. Prior to melting the NTT alloy, high purity titanium was used to remove as much residual gas as possible from the furnace.
